# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 23 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 23 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_023_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 23

**23:1** The next morning the priests were assembled for the dawn sacrifice, waiting for Zechariah to come out and give them his blessing as he always did. He didn't appear. Minutes passed, then longer. One priest finally worked up the courage to step inside — and he found it: dark, coagulated blood, pooled beside the altar of the Lord. And from somewhere a voice spoke: "Zechariah has been killed. His blood will cry out from this place until the one who comes to avenge him arrives."

**23:2** The priest staggered out, white with shock, and told the others everything he had seen and heard. Steeling themselves, they all went in together. They saw. The carved wooden panels of the sanctuary walls groaned and cried out. The priests ripped their robes from neck to hem.

**23:3** They searched for Zechariah's body but couldn't find it. What they found instead was his blood — hardened into stone. Shaken, they went out and broke the news to the people: Zechariah was dead. The grief spread through all Israel. Every tribe mourned and wept for three days and three nights.

**23:4** On the third day, the priests gathered to choose his successor. They cast lots and the lot fell to Simeon — the same Simeon who had been told by the Holy Spirit that he would not die before he had seen the Messiah with his own eyes.
